Cautiously positive overall, but the July 2017 SLOOS tempers the tone. While the FOMC highlights solid job gains and begins balance sheet normalization, banks reported weaker demand across CRE (including construction, land development, and multifamily) and consumer loans (auto and credit cards), alongside tighter standards for consumer credit. Mortgage-related standards eased, partially offsetting this softness, and demand for some nonfarm nonresidential loans was unchanged. Foreign banks reported tighter standards for C&I and CRE. These mixed-to-soft credit dynamics are consistent with below-target inflation and reinforce the Committee’s gradualism, reducing the hawkish tilt implied by labor strength and normalization.
